description: The lease table of a DHCP server: data source 4. Several providers may be active at once (one server per scope). Each stores what its server reports into the leases plugin's table, plugin_leases.dhcp_lease, which grants it the table (ADR 0020 wave 4); the clients plugin runs the client identity cascade on what they report.

cadences.basis: Survey, data source 4, "Sustainable polling frequency": leases change on the scale of minutes to hours, the table is small, and the Kea path costs a control-agent round trip.

page_size.basis: 500 is the figure the collectors carried as a constant before the page became a setting, and nothing more: a documented starting point, not a measurement and not a survey figure. What an installation needs depends on how fast its sources write, which only that installation can measure: the collection surface measures it and suggests a pair. The default is within what the firewall serves for this read, so a database with no row never asks for a page the firewall would cut short.

sizing.basis: The lease searches are grid searches, whose `rowCount` is the page size and `-1` means all rows ("Pagination envelope"): nothing on the firewall's side caps the page. A lease row records when opnview saw it and no other instant of its own, so the lease table is measured on one clock.

functions.description: Called at every probe round: asks the firewall whether this implementation can be read and whether its configuration serves clients.
functions.name: probe

functions.description: Called at every lease pass: reads the server's current lease table and answers one row per lease generation for the leases plugin's table, under rows["leases.dhcp_lease"]: provider_id the provider's id as handed, backend the provider key, address, mac (lower-cased, six colon-separated octets or absent), hostname, dhcp_client_id, duid, iaid, vendor_hint, lease_state (active, expired, reserved or unknown), interface_identifier and interface_device as the server names them, starts_at only when the server reports one, expires_at, observed_at the pass's instant.
functions.name: collect
